text:
Elias Lindholm has given Boston more than his reputation suggested. He has 17 points in 22 games and ranks 25th of 547 skaters in our wins added (how much his goals moved Boston's chances of winning), helped by the overtime winner against Chicago on Oct 31.

The catch is the shooting. Seven goals on 5.7 expected, a 17.9% shooting rate against a talent range centred near 14%. His own chances, 0.91 expected goals per 60, are about what they were last season. That's a player finishing hot, not one suddenly getting to better ice.

The rest of the picture is solid. The Bruins take 58.6% of expected goals with him on at five on five, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 23% of his setups crossing the royal road last season, against 7% for a typical forward. That's the pass that moves a goalie side to side.

What to watch: he has no goals in his last five games while his ice time has climbed. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, mostly on defense, so how the chances against hold up matters as much as the scoring.
headline: Lindholm's finishing has outrun his chances
